question.problem:
An inner product on $V={R}^{3}$ is defined as $⟨x,y⟩=3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+5{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.$ 
Calculate the norm of the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ under this inner product.
question.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $v$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖=\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $‖v‖$ using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{⟨v,v⟩} \\  & =\sqrt{3\cdot (1\cdot 1)+5\cdot ((-1)\cdot (-2))+2\cdot 2} \\  & =\sqrt{3+5+4} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
